objectives: Design a 3-layer test pyramid combining APIRequestContext, page.route() mocks, and real Playwright UI assertions
Know when to hit a real FastAPI backend vs mock slow or non-deterministic LLM responses

sections.title: 1. The 3-Layer AI Testing Pyramid: UI + API + Network Mock
sections.body:
Pure E2E browser tests that hit real LLMs for every button click are slow, expensive, and flaky. Senior engineers combine three Playwright tools:

1. **`APIRequestContext`** (`request.post('/v1/rag/ingest')`) — seed test documents, verify Pydantic/Zod status codes, and clean up test tenants in milliseconds without opening a browser.
2. **`page.route()`** — intercept browser HTTP calls to `/v1/chat` or `/v1/llm` and inject deterministic JSON, HTTP `429 Retry-After`, or `503` timeouts to test UI resilience.
3. **Full E2E Smoke** — run a small tagged `@smoke` suite against the real FastAPI + Vector DB stack before release.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  SEED["1. APIRequestContext: Seed Tenant & Auth Cookie (40 ms)"] --> UI["2. Playwright Page: Open App with Pre-Authenticated State"]
  UI --> ROUTE{"3. page.route() Intercept?"}
  ROUTE -->|"Deterministic Suite"| MOCK["Return Fixture / Inject 429 or 500"]
  ROUTE -->|"Nightly Smoke"| REAL["Hit Live FastAPI + RAG Backend"]
  MOCK --> ASSERT["Web-First Expect + Schema Assertion"]
  REAL --> ASSERT
```

diagrams.title: Network Interception with page.route() for Deterministic AI & Error Tests
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  UI["Browser UI fetch('/v1/chat')"] --> INT{"page.route('**/v1/chat')"}
  INT -->|"Mock 200"| FAKE["route.fulfill(deterministic JSON)"]
  INT -->|"Inject fault"| ERR["route.fulfill(429 Retry-After / 503)"]
  INT -->|"Modify live"| PATCH["route.fetch() -> inspect/override -> fulfill"]
  FAKE --> UI
  ERR --> UI
diagrams.explain: Intercepting `/v1/chat` with **`page.route()`** lets browser E2E tests verify streaming error banners, retry countdowns, and malformed-JSON fallbacks deterministically in milliseconds — zero live LLM cost or flakiness.

diagrams.title: BDD Gherkin -> Step Bindings -> Sharded Docker CI Gate
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  FEAT["login.feature (Given / When / Then)"] --> STEP["Step Definitions (Cucumber.js / pytest-bdd)"]
  STEP --> POM["Playwright POM + BrowserContext"]
  POM -->|"CI Matrix Shards 1..4"| ART["Trace Viewer + HTML/JUnit + Video on Retry"]
  ART --> GATE{"Quality Gate Passed?"}
diagrams.explain: Gherkin describes **what** business behavior matters, while **Step Definitions** delegate UI work to Page Objects. Running across sharded official Playwright Docker images with `trace: 'on-first-retry'` gives instant timeline + DOM + network replay for any CI failure.
